items.title: As Sisonke held what police say was an IED, she waited for them to act
items.description: When Sisonke picked up a device that looked like a glass jar in Perth on Australia Day, she had a sense of foreboding so she took it to police. She says they took some time to act.

items.title: Australian with ISIS links in Syria temporarily blocked from coming home
items.description: The federal government has temporarily banned an Australian citizen linked to ISIS fighters from returning home from Syria.

items.title: 'It was an error': Former Coles cookies manager grilled over Shapes pricing
items.description: A former Coles manager has given evidence in the federal court on day three of a bombshell case between the consumer watchdog and supermarket giant.

items.title: Sydney mental health patients who fled care accused of killing three people
items.description: A driver charged over a double-fatal crash used a staff pass to escape hospital the day before an alleged Sydney stabber fled the same mental health facility.

items.title: Victoria loses MotoGP after almost 30 years at Phillip Island
items.description: Victoria loses the rights to host the Australian Motorcycle Grand Prix, ending a three-decade association with the event.

items.title: Live: Australia's Scott, Willcox up in aerials final, Hickman up later in slopestyle final
items.description: Australia's Danielle Scott and Abbey Willcox are through to the final of the women's aerials at Livigno, with Ally Hickman still to contest the women's slopestyle final on day 12 at the Winter Olympics. Follow live.

items.title: Chalmers's Lowe blow after ex-RBA governor offers rebuke of 'handouts'
items.description: Treasurer Jim Chalmers says Philip Lowe was critical of the government over spending because it did not re-appoint him as RBA governor.

items.title: At Trump's first Gaza board meeting, another leader will be closely watched
items.description: Ahead of the inaugural meeting of US President Donald Trump's Board of Peace, charged with leading the way forward in Gaza, Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto faces perhaps his most significant foreign policy test yet.

items.title: Almost 60 arrested after weeks of violent unrest in NT community
items.description: Northern Territory police have arrested 58 people in relation to weeks of unrest in the remote Top End community, which has seen brawls involving up to a few hundred of people — some of them armed — spilling out onto the streets.

items.title: 'Complete keyboard warrior' sentenced for 'unsavoury' posts about police officer
items.description: A man who a court heard fell victim to an "explosion" of extremist views and misinformation has been convicted of stalking and intimidating a Hunter Valley police officer.

items.title: Alcoa hit with record fine for clearing world's only jarrah forests
items.description: US mining giant Alcoa is forced to pay $55 million after unlawfully clearing parts of a Western Australian native forest to mine bauxite.

items.title: Mazda, Nissan and others face heavy penalties under emission laws
items.description: Major car brands are staring down the barrel of multi-million-dollar penalties for exceeding their emissions, the first results of the federal government's climate laws for new vehicles have revealed.

items.title: Hanson issues partial apology for suggestion there are no 'good' Muslims
items.description: The One Nation leader qualified her earlier remarks, which had been met with condemnation, while reiterating calls for tougher vetting processes for Muslim migrants.

items.title: Career of ex-A-League star 'effectively over' after card fixing sentence
items.description: Former Macarthur FC captain Ulises Dávila avoids jail time over his involvement in a card fixing scandal.

items.title: Sydney man jailed for antisemitic speech in bid 'to deter others'
items.description: Brandan Koschel is jailed after pleading guilty to inciting hatred on the grounds of race during an Australia Day protest in Sydney.

items.title: Colbert on the problem guest CBS 'clearly doesn't want us to talk about'
items.description: The Late Show host's on-air revelation that network executives refused to let him interview a Democratic Senate candidate puts a spotlight on how US media outlets treat political coverage.

items.title: Rescuers reach six skiers in California avalanche, nine more missing
items.description: Rescue crews battle blizzard conditions to reach back-country skiers who survived the avalanche but were left trapped by its snow and ice.

items.title: What experts say about staying together for the children
items.description: When a relationships breaks down, sometimes we think staying in the familiar discomfort is less scary — and even protective — for our kids. But is it ever a good idea to stay in an unhappy relationship for the sake of the children?

items.title: Rocks thrown through glass door cause panic at defence industry event in Canberra
items.description: Officers are looking for two men who fled on bikes after rocks smashed a glass door, causing panic at a defence industry event in Canberra.

items.title: Human remains discovered during building work in Victoria's north
items.description: An investigation is underway after bones were found during construction works for a $13.3-million project at Echuca.

items.title: Man fined $30,000 for poaching rare Queensland rainforest python
items.description: The court heard Clinton Spiteri was with two others when he visited a rainforest in the Cape York area to steal eight snakes.

items.title: ‘Enjoy your dim sum’: Labor accuses Nationals MP of racist taunt
items.description: WA Labor MPs call on a Nationals member to apologise for what they say was a racist comment directed at one of their colleagues.

items.title: Mechanic missing in outback Queensland is rescued after almost a week
items.description: A man in his 40s has been rescued after going missing in outback Queensland for almost a week.

items.title: Who's to blame for Australia's T20 World Cup crash out?
items.description: For the first time since 2009, Australia won't advance from the group stage of a cricket World Cup and some of the game's greatest ever players are demanding answers.

items.title: Ex-cop granted bail over alleged stalking following neighbour dispute
items.description: A former Queensland police officer accused of allegedly wearing a balaclava and Easter bonnet to harass and intimidate a neighbouring family has been granted bail.
